Claim 11 (Currently amended): A method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; __providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm executed on a computer__; and __executing the selected machine learning algorithm on the computer using the pseudo partial ordering, wherein the execution trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model__.

Claim 12 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter; __wherein the property of interest is determined by measuring or calculating a relative ordering or ranking of the molecules based on the property of interest__.

Claim 13 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm __executed on a computer to process the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules__.

Claim 14 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a kernel based learning algorithm __executed on a computer to process the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules__.

Claim 15 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof __modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs and executed on a computer__.

Claim 16 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, an area above, or below, a receiver operator characteristic curve __by processing the pseudo-partial ordering of molecules on a computer__.

Claim 17 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering __by processing the pseudo-partial ordering on a computer__.

Claim 19 (Currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules __using a computer__, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included the pseudo-partial ordering; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering __using a computer__.

Claim 20 (Previously presented): The method of claim 11, wherein a threshold value or cutoff molecule is selected for the molecular proprieties model and used to create a classification model.

Claim 21 (Previously presented): The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest.

Claim 22 (Previously presented): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations.

Claim 23 (Previously presented): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds or substituent groups of the same molecule and the property of interest is a property of the atoms, bonds or substituent groups.

Claim 35 (Currently amended): A __non-transitory__ computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm; providing the pseudo partial ordering of molecules to the selected machine learning algorithm; and executing the selected machine learning algorithm using the pseudo partial ordering, wherein the execution trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.
